captions.instagram:
How does a wall clock work?

A falling weight, a train of gears, and a pendulum that lets them move one tooth per swing. Take a clock apart in 3D, follow the escapement tick by tick, and see why a hot day makes it lose ten seconds.

→ A pendulum clock does not measure time. It counts swings.
→ Inside: a falling weight, a train of gears, an escapement and a pendulum.
→ A pendulum 99.4 cm long takes exactly one second per swing, whatever its bob weighs.
→ Its timing depends only on length and gravity: make it a quarter as long and it ticks twice as fast.
→ The escapement lets the gears move one tooth per swing: lock, push, drop, tick.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/clockclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a wall clock work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A falling weight, a train of gears, and a pendulum that lets them move one tooth per swing. Take a clock apart in 3D, follow the escapement tick by tick, and see why a hot day makes it lose ten seconds.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/clockclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/clockclear

In this video:
• A clock counts swings. A pendulum clock has five parts in a row: a weight or spring for power, a train of gears, an escapement, a pendulum and the hands.
• The pendulum keeps the beat. A pendulum's period is 2π times the square root of its length over gravity.
• The escapement: lock, push, drop. The anchor rocks with the pendulum and catches the escape wheel's teeth on two pallets.
• Gears do the arithmetic. Wheels of 96, 60 and 56 teeth drive pinions of 8, 8 and 7.
• Two hands, one centre, and a bell. Behind the dial, four wheels (36, 36, 6 and 72 teeth) turn the hour hand exactly 12 times slower than the minute hand around the same centre.
• The clock on your wall. Most wall clocks now replace the pendulum with a quartz crystal vibrating 32,768 times a second.
